newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products mixed, weather lifts new crop.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products mixed, weather lifts new crop.

text.p: CBOT soy product futures opened mixed on Tuesday with new crop months higher on forecasts for hot, dry weather in the U.S. Midwest, pit sources said.

Meteorologists predicted temperatures would rise into the 90s (degrees Fahrenheit) this week with no rain expected until Friday. Hot, dry weather can stress soybean crops and a prolonged lack of moisture and heat stress can lead to yield reductions.
Traders also noted USDA Monday said the U.S. soybean crop as of Sunday was 66 percent good to excellent, below the 68 percent in that category the previous week.
At 0959 CDT, soymeal was up $0.30 per ton to down $1.20 with December up $0.10 at $202.30. Soyoil was down 0.16 cent per lb to up 0.02 with December down 0.06 at 22.57.
